learning_objective: 🎯 Compile your creative journey! Learn how to curate your best work into a professional portfolio and connect art with other school subjects.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: A portfolio is a carefully organized folder or digital gallery containing a selection of an artist's best and most diverse work. It shows your skills, style, and progress over time to teachers or colleges.

Art isn't isolated! Art integration means using art to understand other subjects. For example, drawing a diagram of the human heart (Science + Art) or exploring the geometry of Islamic tiles (Math + Art).
You don't put every single sketch in a portfolio. Curation is the process of selecting only your strongest pieces. A good portfolio shows a variety of mediums (pencil, paint, digital, clay).
How you present your work is as important as the work itself. Artworks should be neat, mounted on clean borders (matting), properly labeled with a title and date, and photographed clearly if digital.
A crucial part of a project is looking back at it. Reflection means writing down what inspired you, what challenges you faced while making the art, and how you can improve next time.

fun_activity.title: 📁 Build Your Mini-Gallery
fun_activity.instructions: Gather all the drawings and crafts you've made this year. Act like an art gallery director: pick your top 3 favorite pieces. Give each one a catchy title and write a one-sentence 'artist statement' explaining why you made it!

exam_tips: 📌 Define an Art Portfolio: A curated collection of an artist's best work demonstrating their skills and growth.
📌 Give an example of Art Integration in your answers (e.g., using folk art to learn about the geography and culture of a specific state).
📌 Remember the key steps of portfolio building: Create, Curate (Select), Present, and Reflect.
quick_recap: ⭐ A portfolio should show a progression of your skills from the beginning of the year to the end.
⭐ Art integration makes learning complex subjects in Science, History, or Math more visual and enjoyable.
⭐ Writing an 'Artist Statement' helps viewers understand the meaning and emotion behind your artwork.
